items.label: Property and exit conditions
items.text: The CIU describes approved property from $300,000 and a five-year resale restriction, subject to its alternative-approved-property exception. It warns that the property transaction can lengthen processing. Approval for CBI does not establish the asset’s market value or resale liquidity.

items.label: EU phase-out request
items.text: The government’s 7 July statement reports a Commission request to phase out the programme by 1 June 2028, while saying the programme will continue. This verifies the reported request; it is not an enacted closure or proof that visa-free travel has already been suspended.

afterApproval.label: Visits and citizenship retention
afterApproval.text: The CIU says deprivation of citizenship may occur if the citizen does not spend at least five days in Antigua and Barbuda during the first five calendar years after citizenship, without repayment of the original investment, contribution or purchase price. Keep visit records. This retention condition is separate from the passport’s expiry date.

afterApproval.label: Passport renewal
afterApproval.text: The current CIU passport page describes an initial five-year passport and consideration for renewal subject to five days spent in the country during that period since citizenship. Obtain current renewal instructions and charges. The May 2020 AB10 form is a dated reference: this review did not establish its present fee schedule or procedural applicability, and the current forms index does not list it. That omission does not prove withdrawal.

afterApproval.label: Property holding
afterApproval.text: The current property page restricts resale until five years after purchase, with an exception for purchasing an alternative officially approved property. Preserve title and payment documents and obtain advice before any early disposal. The holding period runs from purchase, whereas the visit condition runs from citizenship.

afterApproval.label: Evidence to retain
afterApproval.text: AB10 version 3 May 2020 illustrates retained-investment evidence for property/business, title or share-register documents, proof of visits and declarations about changes after citizenship. Keep your certificate, ownership and visit records, and ask which current documents are required. These are useful records to retain; the older checklist and its charges are not presented as a newly confirmed renewal procedure.

paymentRisk.label: Submission versus approval
paymentRisk.text: The current CIU fee page requires non-refundable due diligence and 10% of the processing fee on submission. For approved property, the property page places the processing balance and sums due to the developer after approval under the purchase agreement. Obtain written terms for withdrawal, rejection and developer default; do not infer a universal contractual refund from the government fee rules.
